outputs.explanation: Panel A is a schematic (breast anatomy drawing) plus a classification table listing breast cancer subtypes, biomarkers and frequencies; it contains no bar chart or averaged plot requiring individual data points.
Panel B is a schematic diagram illustrating the study aim (circadian phenotypes vs. drug sensitivity/tumor growth); no quantitative plot is present.
Panel C is a schematic showing the experimental setup for measuring circadian rhythms (clock-gene luciferase reporters and recording apparatus); no data plot is shown.

Panel D shows idealized example traces (Model #1-3) used purely to illustrate the stationary/non-stationary analysis workflow, not measured data; this counts as a schematic illustration rather than a data plot, so the check does not apply.
Panel E shows an illustrative correlation heatmap used to explain the analysis concept, not an actual results heatmap; heatmaps are also exempt from requiring individual points.

Panel F contains an illustrative line plot (idealized growth curves for 'Model 1/2/3') used to explain the growth-quantification concept in a schematic overview, not real averaged data with underlying replicates; line plots are also exempt from needing individual points overlaid.

Panel G shows illustrative dose-response curves used schematically to explain the drug-sensitivity quantification approach, not actual averaged experimental data; line plots are exempt from requiring individual points.

Panel H is a schematic showing the genomic analysis workflow with illustrative heatmap and mutation-table icons representing publicly available datasets, not real quantified averages needing individual data points.

Panel I shows a PCA scatter plot and a 3D parameter scatter plot where each dot represents an individual cell line/sample, colored by cluster or circadian phenotype; individual data points are already displayed.
